Read the following extract on the relational data model and answer the questions that follow.
"In a relation, the order of tuples does not matter. Each value in a relation is atomic (cannot be divided further). No two tuples of a relation can be identical."
(i) A row of a relation is called a: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'tuple' as it relates to this theme. (1)

items.answer: (i) tuple (ii) A row of a relation, representing one record. (iii) In Python, a record is a new row; the number of columns stays the same.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) tuple (ii) A row of a relation, representing one record. (iii) In Python, a record is a new row; the number of columns stays the same.

items.stem: What is meant by 'primary key' in the context of keys in a relational database?
items.answer: The candidate key chosen by the designer to uniquely identify the tuples of a relation; it cannot be NULL.
